title: Ember Sprint — Leadership Open Floor & Engineering Pulse
summary: Quarterly pulse emphasizing reliability wins, cost targets for inference, hiring cadence adjustments, and an open Q&A about private deployments and SLAs.
transcript:
[00:00] Samara: Good morning everyone, welcome to the Ember Sprint open floor. Uh, thanks for joining, we have a packed agenda and then open mic at the end. We'll run about an hour, um, and then Q&A.
[00:18] Carlos: Quick thing, I'll start with the infra pulse — overall latency SLOs improved after the KV cache change last week,  p50 down about 12% on text-generation calls, but we still saw tail spikes on longer sequences.
[00:36] Priya: Yep, and just to add, engineering shipped the quantization rollouts to Canary on Tuesday, so those are in beta for 3 customers. Observability shows token cost down ~18% for those cohorts.
[00:52] Samara: Great, that's the kind of unit-economics progress we need. Drew, product?
[01:02] Drew: We're aligning the roadmap to prioritize private deployment telemetry next quarter — customers keep asking for richer audit logs and easier KMS rotation. Also demo prep for the new routing policies on Nov 10.
[01:20] Jules: On private deploys, small note — the on-prem bundle needed a kernel fix, caused 503s in one test cluster, patch went out at 2am, but logs got a little scrambled in the process, so we've flagged the audit trail to be reorganized.
[01:41] Maya: From People — hiring rhythm is slowing slightly for ICs; we're focusing budget on infra and reliability hires through Q1. Also re: org health surveys, thank you for the candid responses, we will share anonymized results next week.
[01:58] Samara: Ok, quick numbers: Q3 ARR growth 7% sequential, net retention 108, churn slightly above plan due to two mid-market accounts. We have one large renewal that moved to next quarter — working with sales.
[02:20] Carlos: There was a customer-facing incident two weeks ago — model fallback misrouted to a quantized variant that caused hallucination regressions. Root cause was mismatch in model tags between registry and router. We've added a preflight check to the rollout pipeline.
[02:42] Audience comment (Speaker 1): Can you explain the rollback process?
[02:47] Priya: Sure — rollback is automatic to the previous variant for a percentage of sessions if the quality metrics degrade. We now added an explicit alert when latency and token-quality drift together. It's not perfect but it's better.
[03:05] Samara: Important note — sales and product please coordinate on messaging for customers who saw hallucination. We need clear incident letters.
[03:15] Drew: I'll own the external comms draft, post it to the incident channel for review.
[03:21] Samara: Thanks.
[03:24] [03:24] Question (Speaker 2): How are we thinking about cost vs latency tradeoffs for Dedicated customers?
[03:31] Carlos: For Dedicated pools we expose a few knobs: batch window, target latency SLO, prefill cache policies. Most customers want consistent p95, so we tune for latency at the expense of cost. But Redwood Optimize recommendations are helping customers recover cost by choosing quantization profiles that preserve quality.
[03:49] Priya: Also roadmap note — in next release we'll expose per-route caching TTLs so customers can pick cost-savings without changing model selection.
[04:03] [04:03] Speaker (All): applause, mm hmm.
[04:07] Maya: People update quick — parental leave policy refined, signups for our mentorship program kicking off Monday. If you're a mentor or mentee, please fill the form.
[04:18] Samara: Quick hiring hotspots: infra (2 backend infra engs), reliability (SRE), product security (one senior PM). We're holding final interviews next week.
[04:31] Audience question (Speaker 3): Any clarity on Private pricing for on-prem bundles?
[04:36] Drew: We're moving to a capacity plus support model, and pricing tiers will be announced after the Nov 12 pricing review. For pilots we will keep a reduced pilot rate.
[04:50] [04:50] Speaker (Unknown): um, will there be a discount for research orgs?
[04:53] Samara: We can do case-by-case; talk to sales ops.
[04:57] Carlos: A quick tech highlight — the new kernel selection heuristics reduced memory churn and allowed us to increase concurrent sessions on A100-like hardware by ~10%. This helps both hosted and dedicated customers.
[05:12] Priya: On tooling, the rollout dashboard now supports canary comparison charts — if quality regresses by more than 2% we'll auto-pause. Small but crucial.
[05:24] Samara: Ok time for open mic, please raise hands in chat, brief questions only.
[05:30] [05:30] Question from Engineering (Ravi): Are we standardizing on a single model catalog naming convention? It's causing router mismatches.
[05:36] Jules: Yes — catalog v2 will enforce canonical names and tags. Migration scripts are queued, target Nov 4.
[05:44] Question from Sales (Hannah): Customers asking about SOC 2 and KMS — what's the timeline for SOC 2 Type II?
[05:51] Maya: We expect Type II in Q2 next year; meanwhile we will share the SOC 2 readiness pack and current controls. For KMS rotation we have docs and integration guides in the console.
[06:04] [06:04] Question from Design (Lena): Is there a brand refresh happening?
[06:07] Samara: Not a full rebrand, but refresh on the website and developer docs early next year.
[06:12] Question from Partner Ops (Marco): Any updates on the marketplace listing with cloud partner?
[06:16] Drew: Listing is in final review, expect it to go live by mid-November.
[06:21] [06:21] Speaker (All): laughter, okay.
[06:24] Samara: Closing remarks: three asks — 1) prioritize reliability playbooks for public incidents, 2) hire for infra and reliability early, 3) help draft customer-facing incident comms. We'll follow up with a short survey to collect feedback on today's format.
[06:41] Carlos: Technical office hours next Tuesday for infra deep dive, drop questions in the infra channel.
[06:46] Drew: I'll circulate the product priorities doc and the Nov 10 demo invite.
[06:51] Maya: People will send out candidate interview schedules and mentorship signups.
[06:56] Samara: Thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.
[06:58] [06:58] (Recording ends)
